senses: Forming a figure.
In Filipino folklore, a fairy, spirit, usually a lesser god or goddess, believed to guard natural features such as forests.
ety: Borrowed from Cebuano diwata, from Proto-Visayan *diwata, from Malay dewata, from Sanskrit देवता (devatā, “god, deity”). Doublet of devata.

senses: An extra or temporary worker in a printing-office.
A grass carp; a white amur.
examples: This grasser had to be pushing 45-50 lb.
Obviously if you see a grasser eat something–a bee, wasp, or mayfly–go that way fast!

senses: A man involved in automobile manufacture.
Taking place within a social group.
examples: Many recent immigrants' marriages are endogamous.

senses: Involving or producing a crackle.
Having two functions.
Of the sky or heavens.
Fiery, made of pure fire.
ety: From Latin empyreus, from Ancient Greek ἐμπύριος (empúrios, “fiery”), from ἐν (en, “en-”) + πῦρ (pûr, “fire”) (English pyre).

senses: Any fish of the bony fish order Lophiiformes, which have an outgrowth they wiggle to lure and catch their prey.
One who practices or defends interventionism.
ety: Borrowed from French interventionniste, equivalent to intervention + -ist.
examples: Senior players were sceptical to begin with, startled by Conte’s aggressively interventionist training sessions, practice constantly stopped by that barking voice, points of positional detail brutally drilled.

senses: Capable of leaching or of being leached
A purported hallucinogenic inhalant made from fermented sewage.
ety: From Genkem (itself from General Chemical), a brand of glue similarly sniffed as a drug in South Africa.
examples: When they cannot afford glue or are too scared to steal petrol, these youngsters turn to Jenkem as a way of getting high.
Billy: You want some Jenkem? It'll make you all better. Sure, it's a natural remedy! Huff on this! Stan: What's in it? Billy: My body waste, silly.

senses: The minimum distance between the two bodies in such a system.
The act or process of denaturalizing, of changing or destroying the quality (nature) of a thing.
A larva of such moth, which when walking alternate legs and prolegs, giving the appearance of measuring
Lacking sufficient sexual desire or activity; sexually unfulfilled; sexually frustrated.
Scleropages formosus (Asian bonytongue)
ety: Borrowed from New Latin, specific epithet of Osteoglossum arowana (now Osteoglossu bicirrhosum), borrowed from Guyanese Kari'na arawana (“the fish Osteoglossum bicirrhosum”; or a like form in Macushi), borrowed, probably via Nheengatu arawanã, from Old Tupi aruanã.

senses: Having a breast, or breasts.
Having a specified kind of breast or covering.
a chili pepper (Capsicum annuum), related to the poblano and usually sold dried.
ety: Borrowed from Spanish mulato. Doublet of mulatto.

senses: A tree or plant that has been miniaturized by planting it in a small pot, restricting its roots, and by careful pruning.
The art of planting and growing trees or plants in such a manner.
ety: From Japanese 盆栽 (bonsai), from Middle Chinese 盆 (MC bwon, “bowl”) + 栽 (MC tsoj|dzojH, “to plant”).

senses: Any savoury snack eaten between meals.
Unevenly; by hopping.
ety: Fanciful extension hip, a regional variant of hop, with the expressive suffix -ity. Attested since the nineteenth century.
examples: Sammy Squirrel slept inside the tortoise's house until nightfall and then he came out and, skippity-hippity, away he went to Owl's Barn.

senses: An Italian prince.
ety: From Italian principe. Doublet of prince and princeps.

senses: Furnished or provided with a sickle.
The singing or the writing of psalms.
A collection of psalms.
ety: Borrowed from Latin psalmōdia, from Koine Greek ψαλμῳδίᾱ (psalmōidíā), from Ancient Greek ψαλμός (psalmós, “psalm”) + ᾠδή (ōidḗ, “song”).

senses: One who does landscaping.
A Canadian two-dollar coin.

A secluded religious community in Eastern Orthodox Christianity which is a dependency of, and generally less physically substantial than, a monastery, generally consisting of living quarters and a church.
ety: From ecclesiastical (medieval) Ancient Greek σκήτη (skḗtē), which is either from a place name in Egypt Σκήτις, Coptic Ϣⲓϩⲏⲧ (Šihēt), or via aphesis from ἀσκητής (askētḗs, “ascetic; monk, hermit”).

senses: A two-legged stand or organism.
Associated with the absence of scurvy; acting against scurvy.
ety: From a- + scorbutic, possibly influenced by scorbic.

senses: Wielding a spear.
One who documents something
examples: But Osterman is not merely a documenter, preserving the lost art form of the radio drama.

senses: Certain plants or genera Solanum, Atropa, and Aralia, with dark, cherry-like berries.
ety: From Middle English morel, morell, from Anglo-Norman and Old French morel, morele, morelle and their etymon Medieval Latin maurella, morella, from Late Latin maurus, morus (“black”) + Latin -ella (diminutive suffix).
examples: It exists in both these plants, but whilst the leaves of the last one contain it in some quantity, none is found in those of the morel.

senses: An advocate of constructivism.
A vertical net, often resting on the sea floor, which entangles fish in the netting, frequently by the gills.
A culverin, a kind of handgun or cannon.
ety: From culverin, perhaps by confusion with culver (“dove or pigeon”).

senses: Bursaria spinosa, a small Australian shrub.
Vachellia constricta, formerly Acacia constricta, whitethorn acacia, a shrub in the family Fabaceae.
Senegalia polyacantha, of India
Ceanothus leucodermis, chaparral whitethorn, a shrub in the family Rhamnaceae.
A diamine, NH₂(CH₂)₄NH₂ (1,4-diaminobutane or butanediamine), produced by the breakdown of amino acids in living and dead organisms.
That attenuates or lessens the seriousness of something, e.g. by providing a mitigating excuse for it.
ety: From Latin ex (“to delete, to cross out”) and tenuatus, past participle of tenuare (“to make thin”) + Middle English -ing. By surface analysis, ex- + tenuate + -ing.

senses: A freshwater dolphin (†Lipotes vexillifer), only found in the Yangtze River, and declared functionally extinct in 2006.
ety: From the Hanyu Pinyin romanization of Mandarin 白鱀豚 /白𬶨豚 (báijìtún).
